query: What should I do if my car won't start?
generated_text:
If your car won't start, let's go through some troubleshooting steps to identify the issue. First, check if the dashboard lights come on when you turn the key. If they don't, it's likely a dead battery. In this case, you can try jump-starting your car. Make sure to follow proper jump-starting procedures to avoid any damage to your vehicle's electrical system.

If the dashboard lights do come on, but the car still won't start, it could be a problem with the starter motor or the fuel delivery system. Listen for any clicking sounds when you turn the key. If you hear a clicking sound, it might indicate a faulty starter motor. If you don't hear any sounds, it could be a fuel delivery issue, such as a faulty fuel pump or clogged fuel filter.

It's also possible that the issue is related to the ignition system. If your car has a push-button start, try using the spare key or the physical key to start the car. If it starts with the spare key, the issue might be with the key fob or the start button.

If none of these steps work, it's recommended to have a professional mechanic inspect your car's ignition and fuel systems to diagnose the issue. They can use specialized tools to check for any problems with the starter motor, fuel pump, or ignition coil.

Remember to always prioritize your safety when working with electrical systems or attempting to start a car that won't start. If you're not comfortable with the troubleshooting process, it's best to seek help from a qualified mechanic.
reference_text: If your car won't start, the most common causes are a dead battery, a faulty starter, or an empty fuel tank. First, check if your headlights and interior lights work; if they are dim or dead, your battery is likely the issue. You can try jump-starting it.

query: How do I check my car's oil level?
generated_text:
To check your car's oil level, you'll want to make sure the engine is turned off and the vehicle is parked on a level surface. Locate the oil dipstick, which is usually labeled "Oil" or have an oil can symbol on it. Pull out the dipstick and wipe it clean with a lint-free cloth or paper towel. Insert the dipstick back into the oil reservoir and pull it out again. The dipstick will now be coated with oil, and the oil level will be indicated by the oil's height on the dipstick.

For your 2020 Corolla, you can find the oil dipstick under the hood, and it's usually located near the front of the engine. Check your owner's manual if you're not sure where it is. The oil level should be between the "MIN" and "MAX" marks on the dipstick. If it's below the "MIN" mark, you'll need to add oil. Be sure to use the correct type of oil for your vehicle, which can be found in the owner's manual.

It's also a good idea to check the oil color and consistency. If the oil is dark or dirty, it may be a sign that it's time for an oil change. If you're unsure about anything, it's always best to consult with a professional mechanic for advice. Remember to always refer to your owner's manual for specific instructions on how to check the oil level in your particular vehicle.
reference_text: To check your oil level, park the car on level ground and wait for the engine to cool down. Pull out the dipstick, wipe it clean with a rag, insert it all the way back in, and then pull it out again. The oil level should be between the 'Full' and 'Add' (or 'F' and 'L') marks.
